title: Short MU — HBM4/DRAM Distribution; SK Hynix Stop Day 1 Leading Signal
entry: Short MU at open Monday July 7 ($950–$990 implied from today's -5.49% session at $976). Do not short below $940 — at that level the day's damage is done and risk/reward shifts. Do not short above $1,000 — approaching the key round-number resistance that may cap the short. Scale: 60% at open, 40% on any intraday dead-cat bounce to $980–$990. Size 3% gross.
stop_loss: $1,035 daily close (~6% above $977 entry midpoint) — implies the HBM4 distribution thesis has failed and MU is reclaiming its ATH trajectory. This level sits just above the June 30 consolidation high; a close above it signals institutional re-accumulation rather than distribution. Exit on the daily close, not intraday.
targets: $900 — prior support from the June 24–28 consolidation range; SK Hynix confirms a second consecutive day of -3%+ declines into a rising broader market; -7.9% from $977 entry midpoint

$840 — pre-ATH breakout support and the approximate 50-day MA zone given the parabolic move from $295; requires broader AI/semi re-rating (NVDA confirmed Stop Day 2 is a bearish sector signal); -14.0%
$770 — full mean-reversion to the May–June 2026 consolidation base where MU spent three weeks before the HBM4 ramp; -21.2%
risk_reward: 1:3.6 to third target from $977 midpoint, $1,035 stop
catalyst: SK Hynix fell -3.38% on July 6 despite KOSPI surging +5.76% — a definitive Stop Day 1 signal in the morning briefing's STEP ASIDE framework. SK Hynix is MU's most direct peer in the HBM4/DRAM market: both compete for the same AI data center memory sockets, and SK Hynix's institutional distribution into a rising broader market is the strongest possible leading indicator of MU's next move. MU hit its 2026 ATH of $1,213.56 on June 25 — the same day the briefing flagged the first HBM4 canary signals — and has declined -19.6% to $976 over the subsequent eight trading days. This is a classic topping pattern: AI euphoria peak → institutional distribution → retail still buying the dip → second distribution leg lower.
thesis:
Micron's 2026 surge from $295 to $1,213 (+311% in six months) is one of the most extreme single-year moves in large-cap semiconductor history. It was driven almost entirely by HBM4 (High Bandwidth Memory 4) demand from AI data centers — specifically, NVIDIA's H200 and next-gen Blackwell Ultra require roughly 8x the DRAM bandwidth of previous GPU generations, creating an unprecedented memory demand cycle. MU, SK Hynix, and Samsung are the only suppliers, and MU was the last to ramp HBM4 to scale. The stock priced in near-perfection: a supercycle narrative embedding $50B+ in annual AI memory revenue by 2028.

The SK Hynix signal breaks that narrative. SK Hynix's -3.38% on a day when KOSPI gained +5.76% is a 9-point spread — statistically significant institutional selling into a favorable macro backdrop. This is the same pattern that preceded the June 25 MU ATH by two days: SK Hynix distributed first, MU followed with a one-to-two session lag. The pattern is repeating: SK Hynix Stop Day 1 confirmed July 6, MU likely enters its distribution phase July 7–8.

The fundamental case for distribution: (1) HBM4 supply is ramping from all three suppliers simultaneously — MU's ramp plus Samsung's catch-up creates oversupply risk in H2 2026. (2) NVDA Stop Day 2 confirmed (closed at $194.83, below the $195 threshold) — this is the primary AI capex driver; if NVDA is under distribution, DRAM suppliers are next. (3) The July 2 NFP print of 57K raises the question of whether AI capex will hold if the broader economy decelerates — hyperscaler CEOs will not sustain $100B+ CAPEX commitments into a contracting revenue environment. (4) MU's valuation at $976 is approximately 22x FY2027 earnings — elevated versus historical semi trough multiples of 12–15x.

The counter-party is the HBM4 supercycle bull who argues: (1) AI demand is structurally inelastic — hyperscalers will maintain capex regardless of macro; (2) MU's -19.6% pullback is healthy digestion of a massive move, not distribution; (3) Samsung has yet to achieve HBM4 volume yield, keeping effective supply tighter than headlines suggest. These are valid risks, which is why the stop at $1,035 is firm — above that level, the re-accumulation thesis dominates.
bull_case: HBM4 demand validates fully: NVIDIA announces 40% upside to H2 memory demand. Samsung HBM4 yield problems deepen, leaving MU and SK Hynix as sole suppliers at premium pricing. MU rallies from $976 back to $1,100 on HBM4 price hike. Short stopped at $1,035. Total loss: ~6% on entry × 3% position = ~0.18% gross.
bear_case: SK Hynix confirms Stop Day 2 on July 7 (second consecutive -3%+ day into rising broader market). NVDA July 7 open shows follow-through below $193 — confirming AI-semi distribution. MU opens July 7 below $960. HBM4 spot checks show Samsung volume yield improving faster than disclosed — oversupply risk materializes. MU reaches Target 2 ($840) by July 18 earnings window.
invalidation: $1,035 MU daily close; OR SK Hynix reverses and gains >3% on July 7 (distribution thesis wrong); OR NVDA recovers above $200 on July 7 close (AI-semi bull regime resumes); OR MU pre-announces positive Q3 guidance above current consensus of $18B quarterly revenue

outcome.note: SK Hynix ADR drew 7x oversubscription with $171.5B in orders from ~1,000 institutions — the largest foreign ADR demand in history. This is the definitive institutional verdict on HBM4 demand: the distribution thesis is structurally wrong. SK Hynix KRX +7.76% on July 9 Asia session. Covering short at $948.80 (July 8 close) locks +2.8% gain while removing exposure to the thesis inversion driven by the SKHY debut.
